key_insight: CASE trains medical agents to actively seek evidence across longitudinal records and MRI instead of only answering from preselected information.
clinical_relevance: This could improve evidence-grounded decision support by helping models inspect the right visits, organs, modalities, and tools over time.
method: Built a longitudinal multimodal benchmark on UK Biobank with 50,401 questions from 4,739 participants.
Used role-specific clinical agents plus a tool-use harness for selecting visits, slices, modalities, and specialist tools.
Transferred workflows from 14,734 frontier-model trajectories, then refined policies with agentic reinforcement learning and self-distillation.
evidence_signal: In matched evaluation, a Qwen3-VL-8B-based agent reportedly improved answer accuracy by over 16% versus GPT-5.4 and over 10% versus Claude Opus 4.8.
watch_item: Performance depends on a complex tool-use setup and retrospective benchmark data, so real-world clinical deployment would need careful external validation and workflow integration.
paper_title: From Given to Gathered Evidence: Agentic Learning for Longitudinal Medical Reasoning
